correctness.rationale: The mathematical census is correct. A fresh independent enumeration reconstructed all \(2^{10}=1024\) labeled five-vertex tournaments, quotiented them under all 120 candidate relabelings into 12 classes, and then evaluated all \(120^3=1{,}728{,}000\) ordered three-ranking profiles. The resulting class counts exactly match the submitted 12-entry table, including 720 profiles for the regular class and 1,167,600 for the transitive class. The source RESULT.md, REVIEW.md and VERIFICATION.md contain literal C0 control bytes that corrupt four \(\frac\) commands and three \(\bigl/\bigr/\binom\) commands in RESULT, plus one \(\binom\) in each of REVIEW and VERIFICATION. The repaired files restore exactly those nine TeX escapes; reversing the restorations reproduces all three frozen Git blob SHAs byte-for-byte, so the repair is transcription-only and leaves the theorem/proof unchanged.
risks: The census is exactly for five alternatives, three ordered voters, strict rankings and the unweighted majority tournament.

evidence: Eggermont et al. prove every \(n\le7\) tournament has a three-permutation realization and enumerate feasibility at 8 and 9 vertices.
Those existence/predictability results imply only that the five-vertex fibers are nonempty.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior literature covers realizability, a strictly weaker question than exact preimage cardinality for every class.

originality.rationale: The closest primary tournament-realization paper proves that every tournament on at most seven vertices is realizable by three permutations and uses McKay’s isomorphism catalogues, but it does not count the preimages of the majority map. McKay supplies the 12 output isomorphism classes, not the 12 three-voter fiber multiplicities. Fresh Resultary and exact-count searches did not locate an equivalent table. Surjectivity does not imply the probability mass function.
residual_risks: An unindexed course note, software output or supplementary dataset could contain the same finite distribution.

evidence: Theorem 1 proves three-permutation realizability through seven vertices; the paper does not tabulate the 12 five-vertex three-voter preimage sizes.
source_inspections.material_read: Complete five-page open-access PDF, including the model, computational method, Theorem 1 and the 8/9-vertex census.
source_inspections.method: Journal full-PDF text plus rendered-page inspection.
source_inspections.title: Realizing Small Tournaments Through Few Permutations
source_inspections.trigger: Direct primary source on realization by exactly three rankings/permutations.

value.rationale: This is the complete probability mass function of the five-candidate majority tournament under the smallest nontrivial odd electorate, refining mere realizability into exact structural frequency data. The full 12-class distribution and extreme disparity between the regular and transitive classes are natural social-choice invariants, not an arbitrary recomputation of the number of tournament classes.

limitations: The repaired public files contain no C0 controls or operational/platform leakage; all mathematical statements and counts are unchanged.
